transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… yeah. I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I’ve been making these kind of stupid technical mistakes at work—things I really do know better than to mess up. Like labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note, or exporting a client cut and realizing the lower-third is the wrong one, even after I thought I checked it.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’m not careless about my job. Or… I don’t want to be. I just felt like maybe I should talk to someone before it becomes a bigger problem.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to—like hobbies, work, or time with friends and family?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, not in a big way. I still like seeing my friends, and I still enjoy editing when things are going well. Maybe I get frustrated sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped enjoying things.

Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed feeling down, sad, or irritable more often than usual, even when things aren’t particularly stressful?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I have normal bad moods or I get annoyed if something goes wrong, but I wouldn’t say I’m just feeling down or irritable for no reason more than usual.

At least… I don’t think that’s been a big thing. Does that answer it okay?
Have you noticed feeling tired or having low energy, even if you’ve rested or had enough sleep?

Not really… I mean, I get tired like anyone does after a long workday, but I don’t think I’m tired even when I’ve slept or anything like that.

I wouldn’t say low energy is the main issue for me. Does that make sense?
Have you found yourself feeling more anxious, worried, or on edge lately, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal stuff sometimes, like work or making sure I’m keeping up, but I wouldn’t say I’m just anxious or on edge for no clear reason lately.

At least nothing that feels out of the ordinary to me. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or staying focused on tasks lately, like during work or while reading something?

Yeah… I guess that’s actually one of the bigger things. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I can still do my job, but I’ve been making these really dumb technical mistakes that I know better than to make.

Like labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note, or exporting a client cut and then realizing the lower-third is the wrong one, even after I thought I checked it. That’s kind of what scared me into coming in, honestly. It feels embarrassing because these are things I should catch. Does that count as trouble focusing?

Have you noticed any problems with your memory or thinking clearly—like forgetting things more often, losing your train of thought, or having trouble organizing tasks—even when you’re not stressed or tired?

I’m not sure… I wouldn’t say my memory is bad exactly. Like, I’m not forgetting major things or feeling confused.

It’s more that I’ll sometimes lose track of what step I’m on if there are a lot of little pieces, but I also don’t know if that’s just normal with my work being detail-heavy. Organizing tasks can get a little messy if I don’t write things down, but I can usually pull it together.

So… maybe a little, but I don’t think I’m having trouble thinking clearly, if that makes sense.
Outside of work, do you find it harder to manage everyday tasks—like keeping track of appointments, remembering to pay bills, or staying organized with personal responsibilities?

I don’t think it’s a big problem outside of work, honestly. I mean, I have the normal stuff where if I don’t put something in my phone I might forget it, but I think that’s pretty typical?

Bills and appointments are mostly okay. My place can get a little disorganized when I’m busy, but I wouldn’t say it’s out of control. I guess I’m not sure what level would count as “harder to manage.” Does that answer it?
Have you found yourself not wanting to do things you used to enjoy, even when you know you should or when you have the time?

I don’t think so… not in a big way. I mean, I still want to do things I like when I have the time. Sometimes I put them off, but that feels more like just… life being busy, not that I don’t enjoy them anymore.

I guess if there’s a specific kind of thing you mean, I can think about it, but I haven’t really noticed a loss of interest or anything like that.
Can you describe how you manage multitasking or interruptions at work? Do you often find yourself losing focus or struggling to return to a task after being distracted?

I think I manage it okay for the most part. My work kind of requires switching between things, so I’m used to juggling a few moving pieces.

Interruptions can throw me off a bit, especially if I’m in the middle of something detailed, but I usually can get back into it once I look at where I left off. I wouldn’t say I’m completely losing focus all the time or anything like that.

I do try to keep notes or markers for myself, just so I don’t miss a step. But… I’m not sure if that’s a problem, or just how the job is?

Have you ever found that these kinds of attention or focus issues significantly interfere with your ability to complete tasks, meet deadlines, or fulfill responsibilities at work or home, even when you’re trying your best?

I guess… yes, at work more than at home. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do my job, because I can, and the camera work itself is good. But on more complex shoots, where there are a lot of moving parts, my producers have started trusting me less.

That’s hard to say, honestly. I think they still like my work, but I can tell I’m not being handed certain responsibilities the way I used to hope I would be. And the chance of moving into a senior director of photography role feels like it’s slipping, even though I know the actual quality of what I shoot is strong.

So… yes, I suppose it is interfering. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you noticed these focus or attention issues happening in situations outside of work, like during conversations, reading for pleasure, or following through on personal projects?

Maybe a little, yes. I don’t want to overstate it, because I can usually keep up, but sometimes even when someone is talking directly to me, I realize I didn’t actually take in what they said.

Like on set, a producer might give me a direct note, and I’m looking right at them, but my brain has already gone to the lens change or the next shot, and then I have to ask them to repeat it. It’s embarrassing, because it probably looks like I wasn’t listening, even though I was trying to. Does that count as the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been experiencing these issues with focus and attention—have they been present most days for the past six months or longer?

Yes… I think it’s definitely been more than six months. I’d say it’s been at this more disruptive level for maybe a little over two years now—about two years and a couple months.

It seemed to really start after the company readjustment, when the way my shoots and edit reviews were run changed. I mean, I probably managed okay before that, or at least it didn’t stand out as much. But since then it’s been happening pretty regularly. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Looking back, would you say you had similar issues with focus, attention, or staying organized when you were younger—like in school or doing tasks as a child or teenager?

I think… yes, looking back, there were signs, though I guess I didn’t think of them that way at the time.

In elementary school, I remember teachers moving my desk around because I’d be out of my seat a lot, or I’d blurt out answers before I was supposed to. Sometimes I’d bother other kids near me, not really meaning to—I’d realize after the fact that I was doing it.

I feel a little embarrassed saying that, because it sounds worse than I want it to. But yes, I think there were some of those issues when I was younger. Does that fit with what you’re asking?
